newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bank shares rise as rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Canada bank shares rise as rate fears ease.

text.p: Shares of Canadian banks rose on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday as concerns eased over a possible hike in U.S. interest rates.
Analysts said the rally followed economic data last week that dampened speculation about inflationary pressure in the U.S. economy.
"I think they are being hopeful," TD Securities bank analyst Roy Palmer, said of bank share buyers.
But Palmer said that even if the Federal Reserve did not raise interest rates at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 to 2, there was still a long-term risk of higher rates.
He noted that Fed officials have said they would be pre-emptive or anticipatory in raising rates to combat inflation.
"If they are going to be anticipatory, they'll be moving before we have any clear evidence that inflation is emerging," Palmer said.
Leading the charge was Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, up 0.75 to 33.75 at midday, topping Toronto actives.

Royal Bank of Canada rose 0.35 to 60.55, while Bank of Montreal was up 0.35 to 53.75. Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 0.10 to 42.60 and Bank of Nova Scotia rose 0.10 to 58.75. Sixth-ranked National Bank of Canada was unchanged at 17.40.
